fig01: Figure 1. Sign crops (annotated ROI, resized to 96 px for display). B = mean grey level, C = grey-level std, S = Laplacian variance (sharpness proxy), px = shorter ROI side. Flagged crops tend to be small, dark or soft, but the unflagged row also contains imperfect images, so the flag is a triage aid only.
fig02: Figure 2. Distributions over the 22 measured sample images with the project-specific 10th-percentile cutoffs (dashed). By construction about 10% of images fall below each line; the cutoffs are triage settings, not safety standards.
fig03: Figure 3. Per-class distributions (boxes = IQR, line = median, outliers hidden, orange dashed = P10 cutoff). Between-class share of rank variance (eta-squared): brightness 0.53, contrast 0.44, sharpness 0.24.
fig04: Figure 4. Share of sampled images flagged per class (bars; whiskers = 95% Wilson interval for the baseline). Overall baseline flag rate 22.7%. Rank agreement with the baseline (Spearman): P5 0.36, P20 1.00, any-trigger 1.00.
fig05: Figure 5. Size and contrast by class. Class medians of the shorter ROI side differ by 0.63 overall IQRs, those of contrast by 1.14; small images are expected to look soft after resizing.
fig06: Figure 6. Pairwise association of the sharpness proxy with contrast and brightness (Spearman rank correlation on the sample). The association describes how the measurements co-vary; it does not show that low contrast or darkness causes low sharpness. Images from one track are near-duplicates, so the effective sample is smaller than the point count.
fig07: Figure 7. Three images chosen by a fixed procedure: the flagged image with most triggers and lowest sharpness; the flagged image closest to its cutoffs (possible false alarm); and the unflagged image closest to the sample medians (reference).
fig08: Figure 8. Counts use ALL valid annotation rows (39209). Selected classes range from 360 to 1980 images (5.5x); the image analysis uses at most 500 images per class, so sampled counts are more balanced than the full counts.
